cases.claim: a mask that weights some cells more than others gives a different score, which is why rounding the sigmoid mask to a boolean would not be a harmless simplification

scaling a whole mask by a constant multiplies the numerator and both denominator terms' product by the same constant, so the score is unchanged while the clip does not bind. The mask's absolute magnitude carries no information; only its spatial profile does
one branch produces 3072 descriptor scalars and 256 mask scalars, and one fingerprint carries four of each
cases.observed: 3072 descriptor scalars, 256 mask scalars, 12 channels, 4 branches

cases.claim: with no overlapping foreground the numerator vanishes and the clipped denominator holds at 1e-3, so the score is zero and finite
a maximum does not depend on the order of its arguments, which is why the branch order is not part of the algorithm
a maximum over three branches is a different function and is not this algorithm
the route score is the maximum over the four frozen branches
the masked cosine of a descriptor with itself, under masks of one, is one
rotating the descriptor by one whole channel block changes the score, which is what shows the tiling is channel-aligned
swapping the two fingerprints swaps the two denominator terms and leaves their product, so the score is unchanged
a descriptor whose length is not the mask length times twelve cannot be scored
as the mask goes to zero the clip keeps the denominator away from zero, so no division by zero can occur

flare_exact_byte_guard.note: Runs beside Stage 8E's generic guard rather than inside it. Stage 8E is closed, so its hard-coded digest registry is not extended from here (spec sections 3 and 52).

runtime_determinism_observed.detail: Non-deterministic cuDNN algorithm selection is upstream's own inference setting. Stage 9A documents it and does not correct it: CUDA, the torch version, cuDNN, repeatability, DataParallel removal and the GPU model are all Stage 9B's.

upstream_declared_dependency_surface.detail: Declared surfaces, not a resolved closure. The two repositories declare different torch requirements and only one of them pins versions at all. A wheel-level lock — the equivalent of the flx bundle pinned by bytes (docs/adr/0072) — is Stage 9B's to build.

score_contract.flattening_order: channel-major: torch flatten(1) over an (N, C, H, W) tensor gives 256 values for channel 0, then channel 1, and so on for twelve channels
score_contract.descriptor_composition: cat(feature_t, feature_m) over the channel axis, texture branch first
score_contract.mask_tiling: numpy.tile(mask, (1, 12)) repeats the whole 256-value mask block twelve times, so block c aligns with channel c
score_contract.mask_semantics: continuous, the sigmoid output; no threshold is applied
score_contract.denominator_clip: (x1 * x2).clip(1e-3, None), applied to the product
score_contract.fusion: score = max(branch_scores) over the four branches
score_contract.dtype: float32 descriptors and masks; numpy float arithmetic

degenerate_overlap.behaviour: as the overlap vanishes the numerator goes to zero while the clipped denominator stays at 1e-3, so the branch score goes to zero

mask_scale_invariance.property: multiplying either mask by a positive constant multiplies the numerator and the product of the two denominator terms by the same constant, so the score is unchanged
mask_scale_invariance.holds_while: the clipped denominator does not bind
mask_scale_invariance.consequence: the mask's absolute magnitude carries no information in the continuous route; only its spatial profile does. That is another reason not to threshold it — a threshold discards exactly the part that matters

notes: A library cosine over the two flattened descriptors is not this function. The masks weight the numerator and both denominator terms, each linearly, and the clip is on the product rather than on either factor.

The paper's Eq. 7 reads as written under binary masks; the implementation generalises it to the sigmoid mask by staying linear in each. Thresholding belongs to the binary branch, which this identity excludes.
The branch scores are diagnostics of one matcher, not four algorithms. A future adapter returns the maximum and may report the winning branch beside it.
